transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’ve lost all interest in teaching and the activities I used to enjoy, and I can’t seem to care about anything the way I used to. It just feels like I'm completely flat and going through the motions every day.
How long have you been feeling this way, has it been for a few weeks or has it been going on for several months?

It has actually been going on for much longer than a few weeks—it's been pretty constant for about a year and a half now. These feelings really started building not long after I took on some extra STEM teaching and club responsibilities at my school.
Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities over the past year and a half, or has it been a persistent low mood?

No, I haven't really had any periods where things got better. It has been a very persistent, heavy feeling that has just steadily built up and stayed constant the entire time. I haven't had any breaks from this joyless state since it started.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about your situation or performance as a teacher, or is it more about just not feeling any pleasure or interest in things?

Honestly, it is very much both. I feel a deep sense of guilt and constantly spiral into thinking I'm a terrible teacher and wife who is letting everyone down when minor things go wrong. At the same time, I feel completely flat even when a lesson goes well, and I've lost all interest in teaching and my usual hobbies like softball and hiking.
Can you tell me more about your energy levels and motivation? Have you noticed any changes in your ability to initiate or complete tasks, or do you feel fatigued most of the time?

I feel completely exhausted all the time, and coming home from school leaves me so drained that simple chores like folding laundry feel like climbing a mountain. This constant fatigue and mental fogginess make it incredibly hard to initiate or finish tasks, which has led to me missing grading deadlines and getting stuck on simple decisions.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or sleep patterns over the past year and a half, such as eating more or less than usual, or sleeping more or less than you used to?

Yes, I've completely lost my appetite and often go the whole school day on just coffee and a granola bar, so my clothes are fitting much looser now. At night, my mind spins with school worries for hours before I can fall asleep, and then I wake up around 4 or 5 a.m. unable to get back to sleep.

You've been experiencing these symptoms for about a year and a half, but can you tell me if there was a specific event or period that triggered the onset of these feelings, or did they gradually build up over time?

They definitely built up gradually, but it all started about two years ago when I took on a lot of extra responsibilities like the advanced STEM track, test prep, and running two clubs. Around that same time, our district introduced a demanding new evaluation system, and the pressure and joylessness just steadily worsened over the next 18 months.
Have you experienced any previous episodes of depression or significant low mood before this 1.5-year period, or is this the first time you've felt this way?
This is the very first time I've ever felt this way. I have no prior history of depression or anything like this before this period started.

Given that you've been experiencing these symptoms for about a year and a half without any significant improvement, and considering this is your first episode, do you think the pressures and stressors from your job and personal life have been consistently present and unrelenting over this entire period?

Yes, the pressures have been absolutely unrelenting and constant the entire time. Ever since I took on the extra STEM track, the clubs, and that new evaluation system, there hasn't been any break or relief from the demands. It has just been a non-stop cycle that matches exactly how long I've been feeling this way.
Have you experienced any episodes where you heard voices, saw things that weren't there, or had thoughts that didn't seem like your own during this 1.5-year period?
No, nothing like that has ever happened to me. I've never heard voices, seen things that weren't there, or felt like my thoughts weren't my own.

You've mentioned no episodes of hearing voices or seeing things that weren't there, but can you tell me if you've ever had any thoughts that seemed unusually suspicious, paranoid, or out of character for you during this time?

No, I haven't experienced any paranoid or suspicious thoughts like that at all. My mind is mostly just filled with constant worry about falling behind at work and feelings of letting everyone down. It is more of a heavy, self-critical loop than anything unusual.

You've denied having any hallucinations or delusions, but can you confirm whether you've experienced any significant disorganization in your thoughts or behaviors that might seem out of character or hard to explain to others?

While I don't have any bizarre or unexplainable behaviors in a psychotic sense, I have experienced a severe and completely out-of-character decline in my ability to stay organized. My brain feels so foggy that I struggle with simple decisions and grading, and my once meticulous home routines and finances have fallen into complete disarray. I just feel too overwhelmed and drained to manage any of it anymore.

You've had a persistent low mood for about a year and a half without significant improvement, but can you tell me if there were any distinct periods within this time frame where your symptoms seemed to worsen or if it has been a steady, unchanging state?

It has been more of a steady, gradual decline rather than coming and going in distinct waves. The feeling has just been pretty constant and building over the last year and a half, closely tied to the relentless pressure and conflicts at school. There really haven't been any breaks or sudden shifts, just a continuous downward slope.

You've described a persistent low mood for about a year and a half without significant improvement, which aligns with both recurrent depressive disorder and a single episode of major depressive disorder, given this is your first episode. Can you help me understand if there have been any periods, even brief, where you felt somewhat better or if the low mood has been consistently present the entire time?

The heavy, joyless feeling has been completely constant for the past year and a half, without any periods of feeling better. Even on days when a lesson goes really well or the kids in the robotics club do something clever, I still just feel flat and can't experience any real lift in my mood.

Given that you've had this persistent low mood for a year and a half without any significant improvement, and this is your first episode, do you think it's possible that you might experience another episode like this in the future, or do you feel like the circumstances that led to this episode are unique and unlikely to recur?

To be honest, I haven't thought much about the future or whether this could happen again. Right now, I am just trying to survive the overwhelming feelings of my present situation. It is really hard to look ahead when just getting through each day takes everything I have.

You've mentioned feeling exhausted and having trouble initiating tasks, can you tell me if you've also experienced any physical slowing down, such as slowed speech or movements, over the past year and a half?

I haven't really noticed any physical slowing down or changes in my speech or movements. It is more that I just feel completely exhausted and drained all the time, so everything takes a massive amount of effort to get started.

Given that this is your first episode of depression and it has lasted for about a year and a half, do you think that if the pressures and stressors from your job were to significantly decrease, you might start to feel better, or do you feel like your depressive symptoms have become somewhat independent of those initial triggers?

I'm really not sure, and I haven't thought about it that way. Because this heavy, flat feeling is so constant now—even on days when things go well at school—it's hard for me to imagine feeling better just by reducing my workload. I don't know for sure, though.
Can you elaborate on how your feelings of guilt and worthlessness affect your daily life and interactions with others, such as your students, colleagues, and family members?

Whenever a student's scores dip or I miss a deadline, I spiral into thinking I'm a terrible teacher and a bad wife who is letting everyone down. I constantly replay my past mistakes, feeling like I don't even deserve my job or my husband's support. It makes me withdraw from everyone, which has only created more tension at home.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide, or have you ever wished you wouldn't wake up, as a way to escape these feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and constant pressure?

Yes, especially at night when I'm lying awake feeling like I'm failing at everything, I do catch myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up or got into some kind of accident. I don't have any plan to do anything to myself, but the idea of simply not being here anymore sometimes feels like a huge relief.
Can you tell me more about these thoughts of not waking up or getting into an accident, how often do you have them and have you ever thought about how you would carry out such an act?

I've been having those thoughts more and more, especially at night when I'm lying awake feeling completely overwhelmed by how much I'm failing everyone. I don't have any kind of plan to hurt myself or carry anything out, and I would never do that. It's just that the idea of an accident or simply not waking up feels like the only way to get some relief from all this pressure.
Have you ever had any specific methods in mind when you think about not waking up or getting into an accident, or are these thoughts more about a general desire to escape your current situation?

No, I don't have any specific methods or plans in mind at all. It is really just a general desire to escape the overwhelming pressure and the constant feeling that I'm failing at everything. The thought of just not being here anymore is more about wanting some relief from it all.
Have you ever felt like you wanted to take action to end your life, or have these thoughts of not waking up or getting into an accident ever involved any intention to harm yourself?

No, I have never wanted to take action to end my life, and those thoughts have never involved any intention to actually harm myself. It is really just about wishing for relief from the constant pressure, but I have absolutely no plan or desire to do anything to myself.

Given that you're experiencing your first episode of depression and it's lasted for about a year and a half, do you think the fact that it's been persistent for so long might suggest that this could be a single, prolonged episode, or do you believe the circumstances that triggered it could lead to future episodes if they recur?

It definitely feels like one continuous, heavy, and exhausting episode that hasn't let up at all for the past year and a half. Because the intense teaching workload, the constant evaluations, and my own perfectionism are still present and hard to escape, I am deeply concerned about my ability to cope now and in the future if these conditions don't change.

Do you think that if you were able to significantly reduce your workload and manage your stress, your symptoms might improve, or do you feel like your depression has taken on a life of its own and would persist regardless of changes in your circumstances?

I'm really not sure. While the overwhelming work stress definitely started all of this, the heavy, flat feeling has become so constant and deep that I don't know if simply cutting back on work would be enough to fix it. It almost feels like it has taken on a life of its own at this point.

Given the persistent nature of your symptoms over the past year and a half, do you think that even if your current episode of depression were to improve, you would still be at risk for experiencing another episode in the future due to the ongoing stressors in your life?

I haven't really thought about the future or the possibility of another episode yet. Right now, I am just trying to get through the day-to-day struggle of my current situation. It's hard to look that far ahead when everything feels so overwhelming right now.

Considering your symptoms have been constant for a year and a half without any significant improvement, do you think the fact that you've had no previous episodes of depression might suggest that this could be a single, prolonged episode of major depressive disorder, or do you believe the ongoing stressors in your life could lead to future episodes if they continue?

I'm really not sure about those medical terms or what they might mean for my future. All I know is that I've never felt anything like this before this current period started a year and a half ago. It's just very hard for me to speculate on what lies ahead when I'm struggling so much to get through each day right now.

Do you think that if the current stressors in your life, such as your workload and evaluations, were to significantly decrease or go away, you might still experience episodes of depression in the future, or do you believe your symptoms are primarily driven by these external factors?

I'm really not sure about what might happen in the future, but right now it definitely feels like the overwhelming workload and evaluation pressure are the main drivers of how I feel. I never experienced anything like this before taking on those extra responsibilities, so it's hard to separate my feelings from those external stressors.

Given that you've had no previous episodes of depression and this episode has lasted for a year and a half, do you think the ongoing nature of your symptoms might be more related to the persistent stressors in your life rather than an inherent tendency to experience recurring episodes of depression?

Yes, I think you're absolutely right. My symptoms seem directly tied to the overwhelming workload, administrative changes, and club responsibilities that started a year and a half ago and have never let up. Because these stressors are constant and have completely worn down my ability to cope, it feels like the ongoing pressure is what keeps me trapped in this state, rather than it being a random or recurring issue.

Do you think that if the current stressors in your life were to resolve, you would be likely to experience another episode of depression in the future, or do you believe that once these stressors are removed, you would be unlikely to experience another episode?
I'm really not sure, to be honest. It is hard for me to even imagine these current work pressures resolving right now, let alone trying to think about the future or whether this would happen again.

Do you think that even if your current symptoms were to improve, the fact that this is your first episode of depression and it has lasted for a year and a half might suggest a higher likelihood of this being a single, prolonged episode of major depressive disorder, rather than a recurrent depressive disorder?

I'm not really sure about those medical classifications or the difference between a single prolonged episode and a recurrent disorder. I just know that this is the absolute first time I've ever experienced anything like this in my life. It has just been one constant, heavy struggle for the last year and a half.
